body.x: GLEC Inc. (Co-CEOs Deokho Kevin Kang and Eun-woo Stella Kim) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time).

GLEC develops solutions that support the measurement, verification, and reduction of carbon emissions in the logistics industry, in line with international standards. By focusing on standardizing carbon data, the company provides a world-class carbon management system and, according to the company, also helps reduce accident risks in logistics operations while improving overall cost efficiency.

As carbon neutrality emerges as a major global industrial challenge, GLEC was selected as a CES 2026 Innovation Award honoree for solutions that support this goal while delivering broad operational benefits. Through this recognition, the company validated the excellence of its proprietary technologies in the global market and stated its intention to expand the decarbonization of the logistics industry and data-driven management worldwide.

With these goals, GLEC participated in CES 2026 and showcased a range of solutions, including the AI-based digital tachograph “GLEC DTG Series 5,” the carbon and driving management-specialized digital tachograph “GLEC Carbon DTG,” and the carbon API solution “GLEC LCS.”

The Innovation Award-winning GLEC DTG Series 5 is a platform that leverages AI and IoT technologies to deliver integrated functions, including carbon data measurement, real-time risk analysis, driving behavior evaluation, and vehicle condition monitoring.

In particular, by embedding an AI engine that predicts accident risks and dangerous driving patterns, GLEC implemented a practical solution that goes beyond simple record-keeping to deliver tangible outcomes such as enhanced driver safety, reduced accident-related costs, insurance linkage, and extended vehicle lifespan. The company also highlighted its highly scalable technology architecture that can expand into global markets.

body.cap: GLEC booth at CES 2026. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The GLEC Carbon DTG introduced alongside it also goes beyond conventional digital tachograph functions, as it is designed to collect and analyze real-time data on vehicle-specific fuel consumption, driving distance, empty-run status, and driver behavior patterns. By applying a data structure optimized for road freight transport environments and measurement algorithms based on the international standard ISO 14083, the device supports logistics companies across regions in meeting ESG and carbon emission reporting requirements. It also helps secure practical management outcomes, such as reduced fuel costs, improved vehicle management efficiency, and minimized operational risks.

The carbon API solution GLEC LCS (Logistics Carbon Standard) is an API-based global logistics carbon emission calculation and verification solution that integrates data across all transport sectors, including rail, maritime, and air logistics hubs beyond road transport. By applying international standards and the GLEC Framework methodology, it supports integration with a wide range of systems, including enterprise-level systems, SaaS, platforms, and WMS. The solution features real-time calculation APIs, automated reporting, and a verification-ready structure.
By presenting this comprehensive hardware-software integrated pipeline that covers carbon measurement, reduction, and safety management, GLEC drew strong attention from visitors at CES 2026.

A GLEC official said, “CES 2026 will serve as an important catalyst for enhancing global awareness of GLEC’s technologies and solutions and for realizing our core growth goals, including global product launches, partnership agreements, customer expansion, and overseas pilot projects.” The official added, “We aim to strengthen our standing as a Korean logistics technology company, secure a foothold for entry into international markets, and build a foundation to generate tangible results in carbon reduction and industrial innovation.”

The Incheon Metropolitan City Government and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority formed the “INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion” at LVCC North Hall during CES 2026, presenting Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as it evolves beyond a smart city into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs, including Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Awards Showcase, the pavilion supported the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES, including 10 companies exhibiting at the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion. In particular, 14 companies won 17 CES Innovation Awards, marking the largest achievement to date and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovative enterprises.
